# `stop_compass_calibration`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Finish or cancel the compass calibration run: with force 0 compute from the collected samples, with nonzero force discard them.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build and 32-bit build, command-socket invocation) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xdc270 (64-bit build); helper stopCompassCalibration (64-bit build) |

Reads optional integer force (default 0). In sampling state (1): force nonzero sets state 2, stops the movement thread, deletes the sampling timer and resets state to 0 (cancel); force 0 freezes the samples, sets state 3, stops the movement thread and timer and starts the calibration calculation thread (reset to 0 if that thread cannot start). If the state is not 1, the call succeeds only when force is 0 and the state is already 3. The calculation runs asynchronously; its outcome is a CompassCalibration event with state complete or fail. The call can block while stopping the movement thread (no finite deadline established). There is no requirement that the mount be parked.

Side effects: Stops the scope movement worker and sampling timer, changes the calibration state, and for force 0 starts the asynchronous calculation thread. Full command-socket calls also incur the shared diagnostic (logging) writes; this is why the strict grade is MUTATOR even for the read-only calls.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"stop_compass_calibration"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional. A missing, null, scalar or array params value, a missing force, or a force of the wrong type (including boolean) all leave force at 0. Unknown keys are ignored. There is no positional form. [READ] |
| `params.force` | integer | no | 0 | Zero requests calculation of the calibration from the samples collected; any nonzero integer cancels the run. Nonzero values are not range-checked. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 207 | State is not 1 and not (force 0 with state 3); the helper assigns no code so the dispatcher default applies. Also used when the calculation thread cannot start if that path assigns no code (unresolved). | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Thread-start failure code is unresolved. Mutex failures throw and are not a documented error reply.

## Example

Request, calculate:

```json
{"id":24,"method":"stop_compass_calibration","params":{"force":0}}
```

Request, cancel:

```json
{"id":25,"method":"stop_compass_calibration","params":{"force":1}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"stop_compass_calibration","result":0,"code":0,"id":24}
```

Reply, not-sampling:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"stop_compass_calibration","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":26}
```
